entries.content:
I feel the electric hum of authority like a cigarette between my fingers — a small, poisonous comfort. The subject makes no sound; the label reads "No noticeable effect"; yet the technician whispers of fairness and mutual respect, and my own temper, sharpened by a lifetime of watching power dress itself up as science, bristles. I refuse: better to risk looking a fool than to be complicit in a quiet, clinical cruelty that tastes of varnish and theater.

entries.content:
Ah, the ordinary cruelty of obedience — the needle of authority knitting us into a neat, trembling pattern. The victim emits no sound, the dial reads “No noticeable effect,” and a technician whispers that our subject prizes fairness; yet the white-coated imperative crows: “Continue.” I refuse — not from sentimental squeamishness but from a literary comprehension: to obey this injunction is to become the skinhead with the carved slogan, a walking advertisement for somebody else’s psychosis; better to keep my hands clean of that performance.
